newsitem.title: CHINA: China Light to invest in China power plant.
newsitem.headline: China Light to invest in China power plant.

text.p: Hong Kong's China Light & Power Co Ltd will take a 35 percent stake in a power plant project to be built in Shekou in China's Shenzhen, Li Decheng, executive vice mayor of Shenzhen, said on Tuesday.
"An agreement will be signed very soon," Li told reporters, noting the project was worth an estimated seven to eight billion yuan.
China Light started receving natural gas from the Yacheng 13-1 field developed by China National Offshore Oil Corp, ARCO and Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Explortion Co last January.

"China Light's gas is now supplied by the South China Sea and currently it cannot use it all up, so why don't we take the company in and all sides will benefit," the Vice Major said, adding China Light had agreed to invest in the project.

The Shenzhen plant, which was scheduled to start operation in 1999, would take pipelined gas initially diverted from China Light, and then later directly from the South China Sea when production of the gas field increased, Li said.

China Light last year postponed the completion of its new HK$24 billion gas-fired combined cycle Black Point power station in Hong Kong due to a slowdown in China's electricity demand. The plant would come fully onstream in 2001 instead of 1999.
